a_restatement: AI agent memory is a structural architecture, not marketing: the system creates memory objects from user interactions and stores them with metadata including timestamps and interaction summaries.

The system retrieves stored memories by comparing query embeddings to memory value embeddings using measures like cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, orders them by timestamp, and updates or merges memory objects when new input matches prior records.

Users can delete memories immediately with 'forget that' or queue them for deletion after a set period with 'forget this after three months,' which solves the problem of memoryless agents requiring repeated input of the same details.

b_answers.answer: Memoryless agents require users to re-enter the same details repeatedly; this system differs by using a structural architecture of memory objects created from interactions, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when requested.
b_answers.quoted_span: Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details; the claim is a loop — query plus memory data from a datastore of your past interactions, into a sequence model, out as a response. What is claimed is structural: memory objects made from your interactions, some on your explicit request, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when you ask. That is a described architecture, not a slogan.
